clues.text: In Egypt, Israelite families used hyssop to brush lamb's blood on their doorframes so the destroyer would not enter.
God told Israel to eat this meal in haste, fully dressed for travel, sandals on and staff in hand.
In the eighteenth year of his reign, King Josiah held one in Jerusalem unlike any since the days of the judges.
Every year Jesus' parents went to Jerusalem for this feast, and at twelve He stayed behind there.
At the table with His apostles, Jesus said He had eagerly desired to eat this meal with them before His suffering.
Pilate told the crowd it was their custom for him to release one prisoner at this time, and they chose Barabbas.
Writing to the Corinthians, Paul said Christ is the lamb of this feast, and He has been sacrificed.
